data.outcome_summary: ICCS 2009 Asian Report presents results from the Asian regional module of the International Civic and Citizenship Education Study (ICCS). The report draws primarily on student data from lower-secondary students in five Asian participating education systems/countries (Chinese Taipei, Hong Kong SAR, Indonesia, Republic of Korea, Thailand), with Grade 8 as the target grade except where Grade 9 is used due to age criteria. Data collection combines an international cognitive test (80 items measuring civic knowledge, analysis, and reasoning; scaled using Rasch Partial Credit Model with weighted likelihood estimates) and student questionnaires including an additional 15-minute Asian questionnaire focused on region-relevant constructs such as trust in institutions, perceptions of government and the legal system, attitudes toward corruption and authoritarian practices, and beliefs about traditional culture, obedience to authority, and Asian identity. The report uses two-stage cluster sampling (PPS school sampling and intact class selection) and reports results as item percentages and questionnaire scale scores, including reliability (Cronbach’s alpha) and item-by-score maps. It also flags that Hong Kong SAR does not meet minimum participation requirements, so its results are excluded from the computation of the ICCS Asian average.
